Togarmah
tō-gär'mä
n. (third son of Gomer; a northern people known in the prophets as horse-traders and as allies of Gog)
From Hebrew Togarmah, of uncertain derivation, appearing also in the fuller phrase beth Togarmah, the house of Togarmah. The KJV renders that phrase literally, which preserves the sense of a clan or dynasty rather than a lone man.

Biblical Definition

Togarmah is the third son of Gomer, named with Ashkenaz and Riphath (Gen 10:3; 1Ch 1:6), and the only one of the three whose people are described at any length. Ezekiel places them in the market of Tyre with a specialty: “They of the house of Togarmah traded in thy fairs with horses and horsemen and mules” (Eze 27:14). Horses and mules, in the ancient world, were military goods; Togarmah supplied the cavalry of the nations. The prophet meets them again in the oracle against Gog, where they ride in from the far north with the coalition: “Gomer, and all his bands; the house of Togarmah of the north quarters, and all his bands: and many people with thee” (Eze 38:6). The picture is consistent — a hard northern people whose trade is war, gathered at the last against the people of God, and broken there. Against them stands the flat scriptural verdict on cavalry: “An horse is a vain thing for safety: neither shall he deliver any by his great strength” (Psa 33:17). The nation that sold horses to the world is finally an exhibit in the case Scripture makes against trusting them.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Togarmah; in sacred geography the house of Togarmah is a northern people descended from Gomer, noted as traders in horses.

expand to see more

TOGARMAH, n. The third son of Gomer, and the nation descended from him.

Ezekiel names the house of Togarmah among the merchants of Tyre.

Their commodities were horses, horsemen and mules, the furniture of war.

They are reckoned with the bands of the north in the prophecy against Gog.

The phrase house of Togarmah denotes the family or dynasty, not a single person.

Key Scripture

Gen 10:3 — "And the sons of Gomer; Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah."

1Ch 1:6 — "And the sons of Gomer; Ashchenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah."

Eze 27:14 — "They of the house of Togarmah traded in thy fairs with horses and horsemen and mules."

Eze 38:6 — "Gomer, and all his bands; the house of Togarmah of the north quarters, and all his bands: and many people with thee."

Modern Corruption

Ezekiel's northern coalition is turned into a datable geopolitical forecast, and the horse trade is read as commerce rather than as the standing biblical emblem of misplaced trust.

expand to see more

Togarmah is a fixture of modern prophecy charts, assigned to whichever northern nation the chart-maker's decade requires, and the assignment is presented with a confidence the text never authorizes. The dictionary declines the game. Ezekiel names peoples his hearers knew from the table of nations; the force of the oracle is that the furthest and fiercest of them can be gathered by God as a hook in the jaw (Eze 38:4) and destroyed on the mountains of Israel to the glory of His name. Attaching each name to a current flag converts a revelation of God's sovereignty into a newspaper puzzle, and every generation that has done it has had to redraw the chart.

The quieter error is to read the horse trade as neutral background. Scripture does not. The law forbade Israel's king to multiply horses to himself (Deu 17:16), and the prophets returned to the theme whenever the nation went shopping for security: “Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots” (Isa 31:1). The house of Togarmah made its living selling that temptation. The believing answer is not a lower estimate of cavalry but a higher estimate of God: “Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God” (Psa 20:7).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Togarmah (H8425), Togarmah; bayith (H1004), house, household; sus (H5483), horse; parash (H6571), horseman; tsaphon (H6828), north.

expand to see more

Hebrew Togarmah (H8425) — Togarmah; the third son of Gomer and the people named from him.

Hebrew bayith (H1004) — house, household, dynasty; the “house of Togarmah” of Ezekiel.

Hebrew sus (H5483) — horse; their trade good, and Scripture's emblem of misplaced confidence.

Hebrew parash (H6571) — horseman, cavalryman; sold in the fairs of Tyre with the horses.

Hebrew tsaphon (H6828) — north, the north quarters; the direction from which the coalition gathers.

Usage

"“Traded in thy fairs with horses and horsemen and mules” — a nation whose export was war."

"“The house of Togarmah of the north quarters” — the far bands gathered and broken."

"“An horse is a vain thing for safety” — the verdict on the whole trade."
